findings.title: Full leaf refund consumes the charge containing the active cleanup receipt before its final access
findings.trigger: Successful owned positive-handle Unregister, or full speculative refund after the locked fast-path recheck (used==0); first-hole error cleanup has the same full-refund structure.
findings.causal_reasoning: The independently admitted readerLeaf contains removal/speculationRemoval. refund binds its full containing charge to that embedded RemovalWork, then ContinueOriginal calls removeStep. removeUnserialized debits owner bytes/pending at lines 277-279, completes governing shrink, and writes the embedded receipt owner/done at lines 286-287; removeStep still unlocks that embedded mutex on return. refund subsequently writes l.debt=0 at registry.go:269. Thus successful full refund ends the new leaf admission before the true last receipt/leaf consumer. Go liveness prevents a memory use-after-free but does not satisfy the explicit last-consumer retained-allocation contract.
findings.distinctions: An unused-branch-only refund while the registered leaf charge survives is a different, covered case. Failed governing shrink retains the SAME original leaf/error and unsettled governing lease debt; this finding does not assert missing failed-cleanup custody. DATA detach-to-original surviving parent is also distinct from ordinary self-refund.
findings.required_correction: Move full-leaf completion to an original surviving caller/last-access teardown seam so the leaf and embedded mutex/receipt remain admitted through their last use; preserve same-owner accounting and retained failure receipt. Do not fix by dropping the debt write alone, since the embedded receipt itself is still used after shrink. Add a control discriminating the final-admission/last-access interval, retaining partial-refund and failed-cleanup assertions.
